experiments.name: Chunk quality - Markdown header-aware splitting

configuration.strategy: Markdown header-aware splitting followed by recursive splitting

findings: The approach produced substantial fragmentation: 56.95% of chunks were under 300 characters.
The contemporaneous analysis attributed this to short Markdown sections and headings becoming independent chunks.
experiments.decision: Rejected for excessive fragmentation on this corpus. The conclusion applies to this implementation, not to all header-aware chunking approaches.
experiments.source_evidence: User-pasted evaluate_chunks.py output and contemporaneous interpretation.

experiments.name: Chunk quality - header-aware splitting with small-section merging
findings: The small-chunk rate decreased from V2's 56.95% to 1.94%.
V3 improved the fragmentation problem but had more chunks and a smaller average chunk size than V1.
Chunk statistics alone do not establish which version retrieves best.
experiments.decision: Retained as a candidate configuration for retrieval comparison against V1. The project later used 721 locked chunks for its retrieval pipeline, but this chunk-quality result alone does not establish retrieval superiority.
experiments.source_evidence: User-pasted evaluate_chunks.py output and contemporaneous interpretation.
